THE BRIEF
From: Sana Qureshi, Cofounder and CEO, Tikau
To: Strategy team
Subject: Tikau: background and what we need from you
Hi team,
Thank you for taking this on. Here is where we stand.
We sell about 7,200 refurbished phones a month through our website, the MegaKart marketplace and six
stores in Delhi NCR. Our phones are good, but people do not trust them enough. Last month a customer
wrote to us: "Phone theek hai, par bharosa nahi hua." We lost ₹1.7 crore at the EBITDA level over the last
twelve months, and our investors expect us to break even in March 2027.
My team does not agree on the fix:
Rohan Bedi, Head of Growth, wants to cut prices on Fair phones and spend more on performance ads.
He says volume comes first and trust will follow.
Kabir Arora, my cofounder, runs our lab. He wants every phone certified and a longer warranty before
we spend more on ads.
Our store managers want a trade in programme, so customers bring us their old phones and we
depend less on wholesale traders.
The board has approved ₹80 lakh of growth money for January to March 2027. The data is in Exhibits 1 to
6. My questions are in a second email on page 7.
Best,
Sana
Company background
Founded in 2021 in Noida by Sana Qureshi and Kabir Arora. Sana was a marketplace category manager. Kabir
grew up working in his father's phone repair shop. "Tikau" means long lasting.
Tikau buys used phones in bulk from wholesale traders, tests and repairs them in its own lab and sells them
with a 6 month warranty and a 7 day return window.
Last twelve months (November 2025 to October 2026): net revenue ₹139 crore, EBITDA minus ₹1.7 crore.
Fixed costs (lab staff, rent, technology and head office): ₹58 lakh a month.
Phones are sold in three grades:
Superb: looks almost new, battery health 85% or more
Good: light marks, battery health 80% or more
Fair: visible wear, fully working
Competitors
PhoneBazaar: the largest organised seller of refurbished phones, with 180 stores and a 12 month warranty.
Its prices are about 6% above Tikau's.
Neighbourhood phone shops and markets: about 4 in 5 used phones in Tikau's cities are sold this way, at
prices 10% to 15% below Tikau's. There is usually no bill and no warranty, and the condition of the battery
and parts is unknown.
New budget phones: a new phone at ₹10,000 competes directly with Tikau's Fair grade.

Performance ads: paid social media and search ads. Website return rates apply.
MegaKart: MegaKart keeps 12% of the selling price on every order. Tikau runs no ads there. Website return rates apply.
Creators: phone review creators paid fixed monthly fees. Their buyers return phones 1.5 times as often as the website rate
for the same grade.
Stores: the fixed spend is rent and staff. Store buyers return phones half as often as the website rate for the same grade.
Referrals: customers share a code, and each order placed with a code uses a ₹350 coupon. Website return rates apply.
Growth dashboard: the last column is what the growth team reports every week: fixed spend plus coupons, divided by
orders. It leaves out MegaKart's commission, returns, warranty and the grade each channel sells.
Contribution after marketing for a channel = contribution of the phones it sells (using its own return rate) minus its fixed
spend, commission and coupons.
Exhibit 4: The lab and phone supply
Lab capacity: the lab tests 8,000 phones a month on two shifts. 10% fail the final check and are sold as spare
parts for about what Tikau paid for them, so they cause no gain or loss. This leaves 7,200 phones a month
that can be sold.
Supply: wholesale traders can sell Tikau at most 2,000 Superb phones a month. Supply of Good and Fair
phones is not a constraint.
Battery checks: today the lab records the battery health shown on the trader's own testing tool. In a
November spot check of 200 Good phones, Tikau's own tester found 22 phones below the 80% printed on
their listings.
Warranty service: repairs take 9 days on average, and 38% of claims need a second visit.
"We are selling phones faster than we can check them properly." Kabir Arora, Cofounder
Exhibit 5: Rules on claims, reviews and data
Every claim must be true for every phone it is shown on. A battery claim needs a reading taken in Tikau's own lab.
Every listing must say "refurbished". "Like new" and "as good as new" may not be used. "Genuine parts" may be used only
if every replaced part is made by the phone's brand. Tikau's replacement batteries are compatible batteries, not brand
made.
Comparisons with PhoneBazaar or any other named seller need data Tikau can show. Tikau has none.
No fake countdown timers, no false "only 1 left" messages and no discounts shown against a price Tikau never charged.
These are dark patterns under India's 2023 consumer protection guidelines.
Reviews must come from verified buyers. Any reward for a review must be disclosed and given whether the review is good
or bad. Paid creator content must be labelled as an advertisement.
No phone may be sold without a completed data wipe, and no phone whose IMEI has been reported lost or stolen may be
sold.

C. Trade in: "Purana do, Tikau lo"
Customers book a pickup and get an instant price for their old phone. Tikau expects 1,000 trade ins in February and 1,800
in March, then 800 more each month until it reaches 4,000 a month.
Each pickup costs ₹400. Traded phones arrive 30% Superb, 50% Good and 20% Fair. 15% of them fail the final check. Those
are sold as spare parts with no gain or loss.
Each traded phone that passes is sold in the same month in place of a wholesale phone of the same grade, and saves
Tikau 8% of the wholesale price for that grade. Traded Superb phones that pass are added to the 2,000 Superb phones
available from traders. Traded phones replace wholesale phones in the lab, so they use no extra lab capacity.
30% of people who trade in also buy a Tikau phone at the same time. They are new customers who would not otherwise
have bought. They buy 40% Superb, 50% Good and 10% Fair, return phones at website rates and get ₹1,000 of extra
credit, which reduces the contribution on that order. These orders do need lab capacity.
The ₹400 pickup cost and the ₹1,000 credit are operating costs. They reduce contribution and do not count against the
₹80 lakh.
How the options work
Timing: setup costs are paid in January. All changes start on 1 February 2027. In January, orders, prices, costs and return
rates stay exactly as they are today, but any setup cost paid in January still reduces January EBITDA.
Combining: you may choose any combination. When options are combined, multiply their effects on orders and on return
rates. Price, cost and warranty changes apply to every phone sold, including trade in orders. The order increases from A,
B1, B2 and B3 do not apply to trade in orders.
Growth money: the setup costs, the third shift and the monthly cost of A and B3 are paid from the ₹80 lakh. Count each
of them once, as growth money, in the month it is spent. Per phone costs (the condition report, new batteries, pickups
and the trade in credit) reduce contribution and are not paid from the ₹80 lakh.
When orders exceed what Tikau can deliver: first, if Superb orders exceed the Superb phones available, reduce Superb
orders in every channel by the same percentage until they fit. Then, if total orders exceed lab capacity, reduce all
remaining orders in every channel and grade by the same percentage until they fit. Orders that cannot be delivered are
lost.

Project DOBAARA: FAQs
MarKSoc DTU Case Competition 2026
These answers apply to every team. Nothing here adds to the case. If something is not answered
here, the case document is the only source. We will not answer questions about whether a plan or
an answer is right.
Submission and general rules
1. How many slides can our deck have?
Up to 8 main slides and up to 4 appendix slides. The cover slide and the thank you slide do not
count towards either limit. The executive summary is a main slide and must be the first slide after
the cover.
2. Where does the decision table go?
In the main slides, filled in for January, February and March, as described on page 7 of the case.
3. Can we attach an Excel file or add links to our working?
Only the PDF deck is assessed. Put any working the judges need to follow in the appendix slides.
4. Can we use outside data, such as real market sizes or real company figures?
No. Use only the numbers in the case document. The real world context on page 2 explains why
the case is set where it is. Do not use it in your calculations.
5. Do slide design and visuals earn marks?
Slide design earns no marks on its own. Clear slides help the judges follow your reasoning, which
does count.
6. Can we write our positioning line in Hindi or Hinglish?
Yes, as the case says in Question 2.
7. Something we need is not in the case. What should we do?
Make a sensible assumption and state it on the slide where you use it. Stated assumptions are
rewarded. Hidden ones are not.
8. How should we round numbers?
Show company totals in ₹ lakh to one decimal place and per phone figures in rupees. Small
rounding differences do not lose marks.
About the case document
9. Exhibit 1 says "More than one answer allowed". Is that a mistake? Do we have to give
more than one answer?
It is not a mistake, and it does not refer to your deck. It describes the survey: each person could
choose more than one answer, which is why the shares add up to more than 100%.
10. Are prices and costs before or after GST?
Before GST, as page 2 of the case says.
11. We have a question about how the options in Exhibit 6 work. Where do we look?
Everything you need is in Exhibit 6. We will not add detail beyond what the case says.
12. Can we use part of an option, for example only some of what B2 includes?
No. Use each option as Exhibit 6 describes it. You may suggest other ideas for after March, clearly
labelled, but your January to March numbers must use the options as written.
Decision table and board tests
13. How do we calculate EBITDA and the return rate?
Use the definitions in Sana's second email on page 7 of the case.
14. Do we fill in all three months of the decision table?
Yes.
15. What does "compared with doing nothing" mean below the decision table?
The difference between your total EBITDA for January to March and the total Tikau would earn
over the same three months if it made no changes.
16. Who decides whether our claims follow Exhibit 5?
The judges, using the rules in Exhibit 5.
17. Is there one correct plan?
No. A team that chooses a different plan from the judges can still win if its numbers are correct and
its reasoning is stronger. We will not comment on whether any plan is right.
Final round
18. Can we change our deck for the final round?
No. Finalists present the exact PDF submitted on Unstop. Slides cannot be edited, added or
reordered.
19. What happens after the presentation?
The judges ask questions. Any team member may be asked, including members who did not
present.
